title: Article 83 — Duration of Houses of Parliament

content.overview: Article 83 fixes the duration of the two Houses: the Council of States is not subject to dissolution and as nearly as possible one-third of its members retire every second year; the House of the People continues for five years from its first meeting unless sooner dissolved, and the expiration of five years operates as a dissolution. While a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, Parliament may by law extend the life of the House of the People by up to one year at a time, not extending beyond six months after the Proclamation ceases.
content.glance: RS: permanent; 1/3 retire every 2 years. LS: 5 years unless dissolved; Emergency extension up to 1 year at a time (max 6 months after Emergency ends).
content.study:
Article 83:

(1) Council of States — not subject to dissolution; as nearly as possible one-third of members retire on the expiration of every second year (Parliament by law provides the details).

(2) House of the People — continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless sooner dissolved; expiration of the five-year period operates as a dissolution. The five-year period may, while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, be extended by Parliament by law for a period not exceeding one year at a time and not extending in any case beyond a period of six months after the Proclamation has ceased to operate.

Examination: RS permanent + biennial retirement; LS 5-year term; dissolution; Emergency extension limits.

sections.heading: Council of States
sections.body: Not subject to dissolution. As nearly as possible one-third of members retire every second year.

sections.heading: House of the People
sections.body: Normal term: five years from first meeting (unless sooner dissolved). Expiration = dissolution. Emergency: Parliament may extend by law up to one year at a time, not beyond six months after the Proclamation ceases to operate.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the duration of the Houses under Article 83.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 83, the Council of States is not subject to dissolution; as nearly as possible one-third of its members retire every second year. The House of the People continues for five years from its first meeting unless sooner dissolved; the expiration of five years operates as a dissolution. During a Proclamation of Emergency, Parliament may by law extend the life of the House of the People by not more than one year at a time, and not beyond six months after the Proclamation ceases to operate.
